Answer: F
Reason: The sagittal CT images clearly demonstrate a sternal fracture and an irregularity/intimal flap in the proximal descending aorta (suggestive of traumatic aortic injury/pseudoaneurysm), while the axial lung window shows pulmonary contusions in the left lung. This combination aligns best with option F, which links mediastinal widening (implied by the vascular injury) and left lung contusions to aortic pathology.
